goal: Re-establish the current event-driven GPU simulator as a reproducible, evidence-backed sm_86 tool on the local RTX 3090 Ti; run a provenance-bound live cohort through correctness, NCU, NVBit, static control data, and sim-run; resolve retained replay freshness; and close one high-value simulator execution seam from fresh held-out evidence while leaving JADE/HETR and CPU-GPU co-simulation deferred.

criteria.description: A current RTX 3090 Ti sm_86 host preflight, release simulator build, and bounded CUDA correctness, NVBit, NCU, static-control, and sim-run smoke are recorded with exact commands, tool versions, paths, exit status, and limitations.

A representative and then six-workload Ampere cohort has separate, provenance-bound correctness, NCU, NVBit, static-control, and deterministic simulator stages; NCU observations remain comparison targets and never enter simulator inputs or tuning.

Current release sim-run replays the fresh cohort and the active retained corpus with coverage, instruction/traffic invariants, readiness diagnostics, typed incomplete tails, and an explicit freshness result; stale outputs are regenerated or honestly reclassified without a workflow gate.

One simulator-core gap is either fixed with the smallest architecture-local change and an untouched-cell validation, or falsified with a reproducible no-go and next discriminator; the handoff explains the causal mechanism and keeps JADE/HETR, sm_120, and rejected candidates unchanged.

The final handoff states the causal mechanism or remaining uncertainty, exact commands and observed results, reproducibility metadata, claim limits, the next GPU-simulator action, and the explicit JADE/HETR, CPU-GPU, sm_120, and rejected-candidate scope exclusions.
